p1: [low, ominous] A serial killer once asked the police for advice... and they lied to him.
[low] Between nineteen seventy-four and nineteen ninety-one, he killed ten people in Wichita, Kansas.
[low, cold] He gave himself a name, and sent letters bragging about it.
[whispers] Then he went silent. For thirteen years.
[low, tense] In two thousand and four, the letters started again.
[low] This time, he asked the police a question.
[whispers] Could he send them a floppy disk... without it being traced?
[low] Police answered with an ad in the newspaper.
[slow, deliberate] Rex, it will be OK.
[low] He believed them. He mailed the disk to a TV station.
[low, tense] Police checked the file. It was last saved by someone named Dennis... at Christ Lutheran Church.
[low] The president of that church council was a husband. A father. A former Cub Scout leader.
[whispers] One of his victims lived just down the street from him.
[low, ominous] His name is Dennis Rader. He called himself B. T. K..
[low, somber] He got ten life sentences. All because he trusted the police.
